basis: A private brougham coachman of about 1904 dressed for the box: a long double-breasted box coat with a shoulder cape and turned-up collar, brass livery buttons and a silk top hat. Cut, length, colour and fit are reconstructed authoring choices; no surviving garment, photograph or record of what Hans Johnson wore is claimed.

garments.name: box_coat_body
garments.note: A coachman's long box coat, its body and sleeves stood off the shirt by a wool's loft, with a turned-up collar.

garments.name: box_coat_skirt
garments.note: The coat's skirt, draped onto his lap, the cushion and the box front.

garments.name: box_coat_cape
garments.note: A shoulder cape hung from the collar's foot.

garments.name: top_hat
garments.note: A silk top hat, its crown waisted a third of the way up and its brim curled at the sides.

garments.name: livery_buttons
garments.note: Two rows of three brass livery buttons.

garments.name: driving_gloves
garments.note: Pale driving gloves with a short gauntlet over the shirt cuff.
